localFacts.fact: Lufthansa allows one cabin trolley of max. 55 x 40 x 23 cm and 8 kg: the Befree Live (40 cm folded) and Peak Design (about 39 cm) fit inside, the AD-01 (89 cm), TP74 (91 cm) and Sachtler (86 cm) go in checked baggage.

Berlin Brandenburg Film Commission: filming on public streets in Berlin as a 'Miniteam' (max. 5 people, max. 1 camera tripod, no lighting set-ups) needs only a Sondernutzung permit from the district; shoots that go beyond common use otherwise need a permit (news reporting excepted).

Koelner Dom: private photos and videos are allowed, but tripods and similar technical aids are not used unless you first obtain an access permit for private recordings with technical aids from the cathedral press office.

German term for the plate check: Sony's Help Guide limit of a tripod screw shorter than 5.5 mm applies to the Stativgewinde; the standard terms are Fluidkopf / Videoneiger, Halbschale (75 mm), Mittelspinne and Gegengewicht.

localPainPoints.pain: Unsure whether a tripod is allowed in cabin baggage on European flights.
localPainPoints.fix: Compact kits that fold to about 40 cm (Befree Live, Peak Design) fit the Lufthansa 55 x 40 x 23 cm trolley; the 86-91 cm video tripods go in the hold.

localPainPoints.pain: Photo tripods move in jerks when filming; German forum users point new filmers to a fluid head.
localPainPoints.fix: Use one of the four fluid-head kits for pans; keep the Peak Design ball head for locked-off shots.
